newsitem.title: USA: USWC prods ease on weak NYMEX, returned refiners.
newsitem.headline: USWC prods ease on weak NYMEX, returned refiners.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices eased in quiet Tuesday discussion as weaker crude futures and talk of restarted refinery units forced sellers to lower their asking prices, traders said.

Four days of weaker NYMEX prices kept buyers sidelined. "We needed bullish stats and we didn't get them," a said broker, referring to Tuesday's U.S. inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
API showed a neutral drop in PADD 5 West Coast gasoline stocks, with supplies totally 1.5 million barrels, off 119,000 barrrels from the previous week.
Traders attibuted lower stocks to decreased production from the region's refiners, many of which remain in maintenance turnaround, brokers said.
Crude futures, which heavily influence West Coast products market, ended four cents lower after API reported a large rise in PADD 3 crude supplies.
Short-covering that lifted NYMEX gasoline futures late Tuesday failed to give a boost to California markets.

Sellers wanted 74.40 cents a gallon for CARB-graded gasoline in Los Angeles, a 0.50 cent decrease from Monday. San Francisco offers were 2.50 cents lower than L.A. material, with few deals heard done in both cities.
Rumors of a restarted gasoline-making unit at Shell's Martinez, plant, relaxed fears of supply tighness and lowered prices, brokers said.
Buyers of low sulphur diesel dropped bids about two cents to 72 cents, and CARB diesel fell the same amount to 80 cents.
